title: Pretendard Mono — Korean UX Spec Folio
description: A monochrome portfolio that reads like a confidential internal spec sheet — heavy black Pretendard headlines on warm-gray ground, with iPhone line-art frames and restrained micro-text chrome as its sole ornament. Distinct from typical portfolio templates by its deliberate refusal of color panels, gradients, or illustration.
philosophy: This design exists for UX and product designers who want their craft to speak through system rigor, not template flair. It refuses gradient, serif, and decorative color — every element must justify its position on the grid. The iPhone-outline motif is simultaneously functional and conceptual: it signals a designer who thinks natively in device viewports. It is made for designers presenting to other designers, in rooms where restraint is the highest form of taste.
goodFor: UX and product design portfolio reviews for design-literate audiences
Mobile app case study decks with device-frame mockup sections
Korean-market design team pitches where Pretendard-style type resonates culturally
avoidFor: Photography or illustration-forward creative portfolios needing rich color
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data visualization color coding
Non-design executive audiences unfamiliar with spec-sheet visual language
Brand decks that rely on vivid palette storytelling to convey identity
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a confidential internal spec document: austere warm-gray ground with a single dominant headline that commands presence through sheer mass rather than ornament. A hairline iPhone outline anchors the right column — simultaneously a viewport reference and a design-system artifact that signals native mobile thinking. The mood is controlled authority; restraint is the credential. Avoid decorative marks, tonal gradients, or any visual warmth that softens the clinical precision — every element should feel as if it passed a grid audit.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a tight ~6% outer margin and no bleed. Title sits flush-left in cols 1–8, anchoring the upper third of the vertical axis; a hairline iPhone outline occupies cols 9–12 as the sole visual counterweight, vertically centered. Micro-text metadata strings — deck ID, date, classification label — are right-aligned along the very bottom edge. No header band; hierarchy is established purely through typographic mass contrast and spatial tension between the text block and the device outline.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a confidential internal design brief circulated between senior designers — austere, annotation-driven, and unsentimental. The left zone is dense and modular, each row a spec entry separated by a hairline rule; the right zone holds an iPhone outline frame that feels functional rather than decorative, a viewport the designer thinks inside natively. The overall rhythm is asymmetric but load-bearing: nothing softens, nothing illustrates. Avoid gradients, filled color panels, rounded decorative containers, and any element that cannot justify its position on the grid.
